description: Pure builds No Sand Beach; the corner office; the memories start going; Earl's glitch warning. Source breakdown: scenes/sequence_03_the_app_breakdown.md (12 film beats, 2:22).
_comment: KEY DISCIPLINE: the memory-loss beats (s03_07, s03_08) deliberately show NOTHING where the memory should be -- no illustrated glitch for Pure's own recollection, only for Earl's on-screen appearance. Sequence 4's beat 4.08 mirrors this by returning the memories as audio only.

beats.display_name: 3.01 Home workspace, night
beats.note: Same desk Sequence 4 opens on -- the collapse in 4.01 reuses this exact setup.

beats.display_name: 3.01 THE IDEA TAKES SHAPE
beats.note: Confident coding -- the deliberate contrast to Sequence 2's uncertain prison typing.

beats.display_name: 3.01 V.O. 'I decided what I got to touch.'
beats.note: "I called it No Sand Beach. Because I grew up seeing that ocean and never once touched the sand. This time, I decided what I got to touch."

beats.display_name: 3.02 THE LAUNCH -- insert on the screen
beats.note: Held silence. No dialogue in this beat.

beats.display_name: 3.02 The held silence after launch
beats.note: He exhales. The thing is live. Nothing has happened yet.

beats.display_name: 3.03 Close on phone, then his face
beats.note: Contents of the offer implied, not detailed.

beats.display_name: 3.03 'Yes -- yes, I can start Monday.'
beats.note: Controlled, trying not to sound too eager.

beats.display_name: 3.03 Wide -- alone in the small apartment
beats.note: Same humble scale as the Seq 2 job-hunting apartment, to sharpen the contrast with 3.04's corner office.

beats.display_name: 3.03 V.O. 'The door didn't see the ten years.'
beats.note: "Every door that had slammed shut for ten years opened on the first try."

beats.display_name: 3.04 THE CORNER OFFICE -- the window view
beats.note: REPEATED COMPOSITION #1 of 3. This exact framing returns in 3.05 and 3.12 with shifting emotional weight -- success, then unease, then isolation.

beats.display_name: 3.04 Pure looks out at Newport
3.04 V.O. 'Just from a different kind of distance now.'
beats.note: "I could see the whole ocean from up there. Funny -- I still couldn't touch it." The film's title thesis restated as irony.

beats.display_name: 3.05 THE NEW LIFE -- window view again
beats.note: REPEATED COMPOSITION #2. Same framing as 3.04, now read as comfort.

beats.display_name: 3.05 Presenting, at ease
3.05 V.O. 'I started to forget I ever had to.'
beats.note: "...I stopped checking over my shoulder. I stopped explaining myself. I started to forget I ever had to." The word 'forget' plants 3.06-3.08.

beats.display_name: 3.06 THE FIRST GLITCH -- close on Pure
beats.note: Something in him stalls. NO visual effect on him -- the failure is internal and unillustrated.

beats.display_name: 3.06 He goes still mid-thought
3.06 V.O. 'I told myself I was just tired.'
3.07 WHAT'S HER LAUGH? -- held close
beats.note: SHOW NOTHING. No flashback, no degraded image, no glitch overlay. The screen simply does not supply the memory, because he cannot. Absence is the technique.

beats.display_name: 3.07 The blank where Delia's laugh should be
3.07 V.O. 'I couldn't find it.'
beats.note: "I tried to remember my mother's laugh. I couldn't find it. Not the sound, not even the shape of her face when she did it."

beats.display_name: 3.08 MARCUS'S VOICE -- checking, finding it
beats.note: Same discipline as 3.07: nothing illustrated. This time the memory is still there, which is worse -- it makes the loss countable.

beats.display_name: 3.08 V.O. 'How many more times I'd get to check.'
beats.note: "Marcus's voice was still there. That time. I didn't know how many more times I'd get to check."

beats.display_name: 3.09 THE SCREEN GLITCHES -- insert
beats.note: First full deployment of the CA-choppy chaotic-rule pattern (RENDER_STYLE.md). Earl's glitch design is a full separate design, not a transition from his Seq 1 memory appearance.

beats.display_name: 3.09 Earl materializes as glitch
beats.note: No dialogue yet -- the appearance itself is the beat.

beats.display_name: 3.09 Let the apparition sit
3.10 Two-shot: the screen as scene partner
beats.note: Treat the glitch screen as a full scene partner, not a prop, despite Earl only existing on the monitor.

beats.display_name: 3.10 'You built a lie, and you're falling in love with it.'
beats.note: Voice run through the same distortion texture as the visual glitch -- warm underneath, corrupted on top.

beats.display_name: 3.10 'You're killing her by becoming a stranger.'
beats.note: "You think you're honoring your mother by becoming someone else?" The film's central accusation.

beats.display_name: 3.10 'I'm not... I'm not you.'
beats.note: Quiet, almost to himself. The one thing he has always been most afraid of.

beats.display_name: 3.11 THE REJECTION -- recoils, closes the laptop
3.11 Closes the laptop
beats.note: Abrupt cut to black on the screen. He is not ready to hear it.

beats.display_name: 3.11 V.O. 'I told myself a lot of things, that year.'
3.12 ALONE IN THE OFFICE -- window view, third time
beats.note: REPEATED COMPOSITION #3, now at night and reframed as isolation. This beat rhymes camera-for-camera with Sequence 2's prison-cell stillness (s02_06) -- the corner office IS the cell.

beats.display_name: 3.12 Sitting alone
3.12 V.O. 'I still couldn't remember what my mother's laugh sounded like.'
beats.note: "I had everything I built." The sequence's closing indictment.

beats.display_name: 3.12 Hold on the isolation
Sequence 3 complete
beats.note: Hands off to Sequence 4: The Collapse -- which opens on this same desk.
